features.title: Workbench information architecture
features.summary: The Workbench's places and navigation: primary and secondary navigation, Overview and its tabs, the single View page, the Workspace pages, the Reviews inbox with its queue, tabs, filters and thread links, the command palette, the Members entry, deep links, how threads recorded in another render context appear and open, and the persistence of the Comment tool.

rules.statement: The primary navigation is Overview, UX Flows and Reviews, the same three destinations in the desktop sidebar, the tablet icon rail and the phone bottom bar.
Overview's Views tab is the only page that lists every View; the sidebar's View list on a View page only switches between Views.

A View's page is its review workspace: it switches Views and Variants, chooses the Locale, viewport and theme of the render context, and shows the View's Spec and Decisions, its Review threads and the UX Flows that use it.
Workspace is one secondary navigation entry below the primary ones, with its own sub-navigation of Settings, Locales and Assets.
Adapters are a section of Workspace Settings, not a page of their own.
The retired addresses of the View list and of Adapters keep working by opening their replacements, Overview's Views tab and the Adapters section of Settings.
Prototype is a mode launched from a UX Flow, never a navigation destination of its own.
The Component Catalog is a secondary area, never part of the primary navigation.
Checks findings and recent activity are tabs of Overview beside its Views tab, with no navigation destination of their own.
Switching Overview's tab updates its address without adding a browser history entry.
Following a link to a Workspace Settings section scrolls to that section, also when the address already names it.
A command palette, open from every Workbench page, jumps to each navigation destination and Workspace page and finds any View, UX Flow or Review thread by search.
Owners reach the Members page from the member menu, and members of other roles see no Members entry.
Reviews is the global inbox of every Review thread in the Workspace, Widget threads and Workspace threads alike.
The inbox's default queue hides resolved threads and lists threads that are ready for review before open ones.
Within each status group, the inbox orders threads by latest activity, newest first.
Resolved and dismissed threads stay reachable from the inbox through an explicit tab or filter.
The inbox lists the threads resolved with a Dismiss group resolution in their own Dismissed tab, and its Resolved tab lists only those resolved with a Resolve group resolution.
The inbox narrows its queue by the structured Review filters, and also by thread author, by threads the member took part in, by threads changed since the member last saw them and by text.
The inbox's filter and open thread are part of its address, so a copied inbox link reopens the same queue and thread.
From the inbox, a Widget thread opens on its View in the Variant and render context it concerns, with the thread open and its Widget selected while the anchor is valid.
A thread started on the canvas, a comment on the whole View included, records the Preview's current Locale, viewport and theme.
A thread's header shows the render context it records and offers to open the thread in the current context instead.
When a recorded Locale, viewport or theme no longer exists, the Workbench opens the thread with the default for it and the other recorded members, and shows a non-blocking notice naming it.

On the canvas, a thread whose recorded render context differs from the current one keeps its otherwise visible pin and bubble, muted and labeled with that context; a member the thread does not record is never a difference.

Activating a muted pin or bubble switches the Preview render context to the thread's recorded members, keeping the chrome, the Variant and every member the thread does not record, and opens the thread.
A thread without a recorded render context is never muted.
Muting never shows a pin that another pin rule hides and never moves a pin.
A Workspace thread has no canvas link; its link opens it in the Reviews inbox.
A link to a View carries its render context, selected Widget, open thread and panel, so opening it reproduces what its author saw.
After a comment target is committed, Comment mode stays on for the next comment until the user leaves it.

- {{R.wb.ia.catalog}}: Not built as of 673d086: the Workbench has no Component Catalog area (no route under `app/pages/`), although Catalog problems of unused entries are to appear only in Catalog management ({{R.checks.catalog-used}}); tracked in issue #116 (https://github.com/DevilTea/uiux/issues/116).

features.title: Device capability tiers
features.summary: What the Workbench offers on desktop, tablet and phone layouts, and how the narrower layouts limit authoring and comment actions.

rules.statement: On a desktop layout the Workbench offers every action the member's role allows.
On a tablet layout the Workbench offers review: the canvas, comments, resolving and reopening threads, UX Flows and the Prototype player.
On a tablet layout the Workbench offers no structural editing; authoring screens stay read-only and say that editing happens on desktop.
On a phone layout the Workbench offers reading the Spec and triaging and replying to comments, and no structural editing.
On a phone no new canvas comment can be started.
On a phone neither the canvas thread bubble nor the Reviews sheet offers Re-anchor or Promote to Decision.
On a phone the Reviews inbox opens a thread in a sheet where the reviewer reads, replies, resolves and reopens it.
On a phone, a fresh load of the bare Overview address opens Reviews, while an Overview address that names a tab, or Overview reached by navigation, stays on Overview.

features.title: Workbench chrome language and theme
features.summary: The Workbench chrome's own interface language and theme: the available languages, how the initial language and theme are chosen and changed, their independence from the Preview render context, and the zh-TW terminology policy.

rules.statement: The Workbench chrome is available in English (en-US) and Traditional Chinese (zh-TW).
Until the user chooses a language, the chrome follows the browser's preferred languages and falls back to English.
The user can switch the chrome language at any time, and the choice is kept for that browser until the user returns to following the browser.
The chrome has its own light and dark themes and follows the operating system's preference until the user chooses one.
Changing the chrome language or theme never changes the previewed View's Locale or theme, and changing the render context never changes the chrome.
Workbench links never carry the chrome language or theme.
In the zh-TW chrome, the glossary's domain nouns stay in English while actions and general interface text are translated.
Chrome layouts tolerate the length differences between English and Chinese labels without overlapping or cutting off essential text.

features.title: Workbench accessibility
features.summary: Accessibility of the Workbench chrome: the conformance level in both themes, non-pointer paths for canvas actions, focus after canvas commits, target sizes and the minimum text size.

rules.statement: A muted pin's accessible name includes its recorded render context, so its muted state never depends on color alone.
The Workbench chrome conforms to WCAG 2.2 level AA in both the light and the dark theme.
Interactive chrome targets are at least 24 by 24 CSS pixels, and at least 44 by 44 on touch layouts.
Every canvas action has a path that needs no pointer.
A Widget can be chosen as a comment target from the Widget tree by keyboard, without pointing into the Preview.
On touch, no action or information depends on hover.
No chrome text is smaller than 12 CSS pixels, in either chrome language.
After a click commits a Select or Comment target inside the Preview, keyboard focus returns to the canvas so Workbench shortcuts keep working.

features.title: Live refresh
features.summary: Server-pushed change notifications that keep open Workbenches current, how clients resynchronize or fall back, and how the Workbench treats remote changes and revision conflicts while a user works.

rules.statement: The server pushes change notifications to Workbenches over a server-sent events stream open to every authenticated member on both listeners.
After each successful commit to a View, UX Flow, Locale, Review thread, Asset or the Workspace, the stream sends a change or removal event for that resource.
The stream also sends an event when a lease is acquired, released or force-released, and when the roster or the member's role changes.
Events never carry canonical content, actors or message bodies; clients re-read what changed through the normal point-read and list APIs.
Nothing is replayed: `Last-Event-ID` is ignored, and a reconnect, or a changed server instance ID after a restart, makes the client resynchronize what it shows from canonical resources.
Commits made through `/api/*` and `/mcp` emit alike, because both run in the same server process; edits made to Workspace files outside UIUX are not detected.
When the event stream cannot connect, the Workbench falls back to polling.
The server caps the open event streams per session, and ending a session closes its open stream.
When an on-screen resource changes elsewhere and the user has no draft of it, the Workbench re-reads and re-renders it without asking and briefly highlights new timeline entries.

When it changes while the user is drafting, the Workbench keeps the draft, re-reads and shows an "updated by others" notice above the composer; the draft's `expectedRevision` moves to the fresh revision only when the user acknowledges the notice.

After a revision conflict the Workbench never resends or retries a write by itself: it re-reads, keeps the draft or choices and shows the new state, and the user acts again, so an action aimed at one state never silently applies to a newer one.
After a reply is refused for a revision conflict, the Workbench keeps the reply, shows what changed and offers to send it again against the new revision in one step.
When the member's access changes, the Workbench re-reads its session and applies the new role to what it offers.

contracts.title: Workbench addresses and deep links
contracts.summary: The Workbench's shareable addresses: the query keys and values that select Overview's tab, a Workspace Settings section, a View's render context, selection, thread and panel, and the Reviews inbox's filter and open thread, and the retired addresses that redirect.

clauses.statement: Overview's tab is the `tab` query of `/`, one of `views`, `checks` and `activity`; `views` is the default and is written as no `tab` at all.
`/views` redirects to `/?tab=views`, `/workspace` redirects to `/workspace/settings`, and `/workspace/adapters` redirects to `/workspace/settings?section=adapters`.
`/workspace/settings` takes the section to show in `section`, one of `general`, `viewports`, `themes` and `adapters`; an unknown value opens the page at its top.

`/views/<viewId>` takes the render context in `variant`, `locale`, `viewport` and `theme`, the selected Widget in `widget`, the open thread in `thread` and the side panel in `panel`, one of `comments`, `inspect`, `spec` and `readiness`. An omitted or empty value means the current default, and `widget` is omitted for the RootShell.

`/reviews` takes the open thread in `thread` and its filter in `status` (comma-separated `ready-for-review`, `open`, `resolved` and `dismissed`, or `all`; omitted for the default queue), `resolution`, `view` (View IDs, or `workspace` for Workspace threads), `variant` (Variant names, or `*` for View-wide threads), `author`, `anchor` (`valid`, `stale`, `missing`), `domain`, `mine=1`, `unread=1` and `q`. `compose=workspace`, with an optional `from` View ID naming the View it starts from, opens the Workspace comment composer once, and closing the composer removes both keys.
